countries.name: India
countries.summary: India's higher-education system is overseen by the Ministry of Education and its statutory regulators - the University Grants Commission for universities and degrees, the All India Council for Technical Education for technical and management programmes, and the National Medical Commission for medical education. International applicants normally enter through an institution's own international-admissions office, through the government's Study in India portal, or through a centrally administered scheme such as DASA for engineering and architecture seats at NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded technical institutes. Entry rules differ by nationality, residency status, the prior qualification held and the discipline chosen.
countries.whyStudentsChooseIt: International applicants look at India for English-taught degrees across computing, engineering, management, design, sciences, law and health disciplines, and for a single national application route: the Ministry of Education's Study in India portal issues an SII ID and lets an applicant send one profile to several participating institutes. Government-funded study places also exist through Indian Council for Cultural Relations scholarship schemes, which are applied for through Indian diplomatic missions rather than directly to a university. What an individual applicant can access depends on citizenship, residency status, how the prior qualification is assessed for equivalence, and whether the programme is attached to a national entrance test.
countries.climate: Climate varies widely by region, from alpine Himalayan conditions in the north to tropical coastal and semi-arid zones further south, with a June-to-September monsoon across most of the country.
countries.metaTitle: Study in India: Guide for International Students
countries.metaDescription: Regulators, admission routes, entrance tests, student visa and FRRO rules that international applicants should verify before applying to an Indian university.

Students study ocular anatomy and physiology, geometric and physiological optics, refraction, binocular vision, contact lenses, low vision, ocular disease and dispensing, with supervised clinical practice. Programmes usually last three to four years, often including a clinical internship. Registration to practise as an optometrist is controlled by national regulators, so international students should check recognition where they plan to work.

universities.name: University of Hyderabad
universities.summary: The University of Hyderabad is a central public university in Gachibowli, Hyderabad, Telangana, established by an Act of Parliament in 1974 and notified as a UGC Institution of Eminence. Its 12 schools teach the sciences, humanities, social sciences, economics, management, computing, engineering, medical sciences and the performing and visual arts through integrated, master's, M.Tech and doctoral programmes.
universities.campusLifestyle: UoH is a unitary university with every school, department and centre on its roughly 2,000-acre Gachibowli campus, split into North and South campuses; a separate city campus, the Golden Threshold, was Sarojini Naidu's home. Facilities include the Indira Gandhi Memorial Library, a DST-funded high-performance computing facility and Centre for Nanotechnology, two food courts, two shopping complexes, three ATMs, a post office and a health centre. The main sports complex has a cricket pavilion, 400 m track, indoor badminton stadium and fitness centre, and a second complex adds football, tennis, basketball and a women's fitness centre.
universities.cityProfile: Hyderabad, capital of Telangana, was founded by Quli Qutub Shah in 1591 and is a large metropolis with a mix of linguistic, religious and ethnic communities. UoH's prospectus notes that the weather is pleasant for most of the year except April and May, when temperatures can reach about 40 degrees Celsius. The city is home to nine major universities and many research institutions, laboratories and IT companies. The campus sits at Gachibowli on Prof. C.R. Rao Road, on the old Hyderabad-Bombay road in the western part of the city; international students report to the Office for International Affairs in the SIP Building on the South Campus. Hostel places are not given to students already living within the Hyderabad-Secunderabad municipal limits, so new arrivals from abroad are generally housed on campus.
universities.practicalExposure: Practical training depends on the school. The School of Computer and Information Sciences follows AICTE internship rules: the M.Tech in Computer Science and in Artificial Intelligence ends with a one-year project in the second year, and the university's Placement Guidance and Advisory Board helps students find internships. M.Sc. Mathematics, Applied Mathematics and Statistics students complete an internship of at least 60 hours, and Integrated M.Sc. Mathematical Sciences students complete a 60-hour and a 120-hour internship. Master of Visual Arts admission includes a portfolio review, and Master of Performing Arts programmes in dance, theatre and music assess practical performance. The MBA in Health Care & Hospital Management recruits graduates from medical, nursing, pharmacy and life-science backgrounds. Research infrastructure on campus includes DST FIST support to four science schools, a DST high-performance computing facility, the Centre for Nanotechnology and the DRDO-supported Advanced Centre of Research in High Energy Materials (ACRHEM).
universities.hostelOverview: UoH has 23 hostels housing more than 5,000 men and women, spread across the North and South campuses so students live near their departments. Nine hostels provide dining facilities. Priority goes to students from distant places, and students living within the Hyderabad-Secunderabad municipal limits are not given hostel places. Allotment is managed by the Chief Warden's office and each hostel has one or two wardens. The 2026-27 prospectus does not publish hostel or mess charges; they are billed separately from the US-dollar tuition fee.
universities.dietarySupport: Nine of UoH's 23 hostels provide dining, and two food courts on the North and South campuses serve breakfast, lunch and dinner. The two campus shopping complexes include canteens, salons and grocery stores. Three ATMs (near the Administration Building, at the North shopping complex and next to Tagore International House on the South Campus) and a post office next to the Guest House cover daily banking and postal needs.
universities.safetyOverview: The UoH Health Centre gives primary health care and emergency services 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, with round-the-clock ambulance cover (040-23132400). A Psychological Counselling Unit with a female and a male counsellor offers confidential counselling. Student services include anti-ragging squads, the Office of the Chief Proctor, an Equal Opportunities Cell and an Internal Complaints Committee (GS-CASH).
universities.studentSupport: The Office for International Affairs (OIA), in the SIP Building on the South Campus, handles international admissions and helps new students settle in, with information on campus services, stay documents and public services. Contact: internationaluoh@uohyd.ac.in, +91 40 2313 4041. The Dean of Students' Welfare arranges student medical insurance and claim settlements.
whyChoose: UoH is one of eight public institutions on the UGC's Institution of Eminence list, notified on 17 February 2020.
NIRF 2025 ranks UoH 18th among Indian universities and 26th overall, and NAAC accredits it A+ with a CGPA of 3.28 (Cycle 4).

International applicants apply directly to UoH and are assessed in absentia on their academic record, not on CUET or other Indian entrance tests, for supernumerary seats of up to 25 per cent of intake.
Tuition is published in US dollars per semester for 2026-27, from USD 1,090 for M.A. and performing-arts programmes to USD 8,775 for the MBA programmes, with SAARC and Korean nationals paying half.

The catalogue is unusually broad for one campus: five-year integrated M.Sc. and M.A. degrees, M.Sc. life sciences, M.Tech, MBA, public health, and master's degrees in dance, theatre, music and visual arts.
thingsToConsider: International seats are supernumerary and depend on the department's Admissions Committee; UoH states that not all international seats are filled in a given year.
The application window is short: January to 30 April, with decisions by 31 May, well before the July (PG) and August (UG and integrated) starts.
NRIs holding Indian passports are not international students at UoH and must use the Indian entrance route.
Applicants who did not graduate from a university in an English-speaking country need IELTS Academic 6.5 or TOEFL iBT 80 or equivalent.
Medical insurance, union and aid funds, deposits and an alumni fee are payable in Indian rupees on top of the US-dollar tuition, and hostel and mess charges are not published in the prospectus.

The M.A. and Integrated M.A. programmes in Hindi, Telugu, Urdu and Sanskrit are taught in those languages, so applicants need strong reading and writing skills in the language, and the five-year Integrated M.Tech programmes admit through the JoSAA/DASA engineering route rather than the in-absentia route.
bestFitFor: Science graduates seeking a research-oriented M.Sc. in life sciences, chemistry, physics or mathematics at a central university with USD 1,880 semester fees.
School-leavers with strong science or arts results who want a five-year integrated master's degree in one programme.

faq.question: Is the University of Hyderabad a public or a private university?
faq.answer: It is a public central university, established by an Act of Parliament (Act No. 39 of 1974) on 2 October 1974 and funded through the University Grants Commission. It appears on the UGC's list of Central Universities and on its Institution of Eminence list, notified on 17 February 2020. It is a unitary university: all schools are on the Gachibowli campus and it has no affiliated colleges or branch campuses.

faq.question: Who counts as an international student at UoH?
faq.answer: UoH treats anyone holding a foreign passport as an international student, including Persons of Indian Origin and OCI cardholders with a foreign passport. NRIs who hold Indian passports are Indian nationals and apply through the Indian entrance route. International students are admitted to supernumerary seats of up to 25 per cent over and above the approved intake of a course, subject to infrastructure and the Admissions Committee's recommendation.

faq.question: Do I need to take CUET, GATE or another Indian entrance test?
faq.answer: Not for the direct international route. UoH may admit international applicants in absentia, on their academic record, if the department's Admissions Committee finds them suitable; the qualifying degree and marks must match the conditions set for Indian applicants. Foreign nationals who studied in India and live in India must take part of the entrance examination as an interview at UoH. The five-year Integrated M.Tech programmes use the JoSAA/DASA engineering route instead.

faq.question: What is the language of instruction, and do I need IELTS or TOEFL?
faq.answer: English is the medium of instruction for all courses except language courses, which are taught in the language concerned. Applicants who are not graduates of a university in an English-speaking country must provide IELTS Academic 6.5 or TOEFL (iBT 80, paper-based 560, computer-based 220), valid for two years. The School of Computer and Information Sciences also asks M.Tech applicants for a TOEFL or IELTS score and a reference letter.

faq.question: How much does a UoH programme cost an international student?
faq.answer: Tuition is charged in US dollars per semester, two semesters a year. For 2026-27, foreign and NRI students pay USD 1,090 for M.A., integrated M.A. and performing or visual arts programmes; USD 1,880 for most M.Sc., integrated M.Sc., B.Optometry, MPH and M.Tech programmes; USD 2,180 to 2,420 for M.A. Communication; and USD 8,775 for the MBA programmes. Some groups add a one-time development fee of USD 1,100. SAARC and Korean nationals pay half.

faq.question: What else do I pay besides tuition?
faq.answer: Medical insurance (charged as per actuals), the Students' Union fund and the Students' Aid fund are paid in Indian rupees every July-December semester. A refundable deposit is paid in rupees at admission, and international students pay INR 360 to the Alumni fund. Hostel and mess charges are billed separately and are not listed in the 2026-27 prospectus.

faq.question: How do I apply as a self-financed international student?
faq.answer: Register on the Government of India's Study in India (SII) portal for an SII number, which UoH requires from all international applicants except OCI cardholders. Complete UoH's application form for international students and email it with certified mark sheets, passport copy, three months of bank statements and two recommendation letters to internationaluoh@uohyd.ac.in, or post it to the Office for International Affairs. A medical fitness certificate is also required.

faq.question: When is the application deadline, and when do classes start?
faq.answer: International applications are accepted from January until 30 April, and UoH communicates decisions by 31 May. For 2026-27, postgraduate classes began between 15 and 20 July 2026, and first-semester teaching for undergraduate and integrated programmes began on 17 August 2026 (21 August for B.Optometry).

faq.question: Are scholarships available?
faq.answer: UoH does not publish a tuition waiver for self-financed international students. Students admitted through the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR) are charged at the SAARC rate, which is 50 per cent of the regular fee, and ICCR pays the tuition and compulsory fees directly to UoH. ICCR and other government-sponsored applicants apply through their sponsoring body rather than directly.

faq.question: What visa do I need, and what happens after arrival?
faq.answer: An Indian student visa is required; UoH sends an admission letter that is used to apply at the Indian mission in the applicant's home country, and processing can take three to eight weeks. Student-visa holders staying more than 180 days must register with the FRRO within 14 days of arrival, and employment is not permitted on a student visa.

faq.question: What do UoH's accreditations and rankings mean for my home country?
faq.answer: The NAAC A+ grade (CGPA 3.28, Cycle 4, declared January 2023), the Institution of Eminence notification and the NIRF 2025 ranks (18th University, 26th Overall, 32nd Research) are Indian quality-assurance and ranking outcomes. They do not by themselves license graduates to practise a profession abroad; recognition of a UoH degree for further study or registration depends on the authority in the country concerned.

faq.question: Where will I live, and what does accommodation cost?
faq.answer: UoH has 23 hostels for more than 5,000 students across the North and South campuses, nine of them with dining. Priority goes to students from distant places, and students living within Hyderabad-Secunderabad municipal limits are not given hostel places. Hostel and mess charges are not published in the 2026-27 prospectus and are billed separately from tuition.

faq.question: Should I choose a five-year integrated master's or a two-year master's?
faq.answer: The integrated M.Sc. and M.A. programmes admit school-leavers with at least 60 per cent at Class 12 and run for ten semesters, with the first two or three years taught through the Centre for Integrated Studies. The two-year master's programmes admit bachelor's graduates for four semesters. Fees per semester are the same within each fee group, so the integrated route costs more in total because it is longer.

evidence.claimText: The University Grants Commission is the statutory body of the Government of India for coordination, determination and maintenance of standards of higher education, operating under the Ministry of Education.
evidence.sourceLabel: University Grants Commission (UGC) - official site
evidence.internalNotes: UGC publishes the authoritative lists of Central, State, Deemed-to-be and State Private universities, plus a published list of fake universities. Corroborated by the Study in India portal Indian Higher Education page, which states all institutions are governed by the Ministry of Education.

evidence.claimText: The All India Council for Technical Education is the Government of India statutory body for technical education, covering engineering, management and allied technical programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) - official site

evidence.claimText: The National Medical Commission is the Government of India regulator for medical education and medical institutions; medical and dental admission is governed separately from general higher education.
evidence.sourceLabel: National Medical Commission (NMC) - official site

evidence.claimText: India's higher-education landscape includes over 1,100 universities and more than 45,000 colleges, all governed by the Ministry of Education, and higher education begins after 12 years of schooling.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Indian Higher Education
evidence.internalNotes: Portal-published counts are approximate and shift between AISHE cycles; treat them as indicative and re-check at review. Regulator identity is separately verified against UGC and AICTE.

evidence.claimText: The Study in India portal is the Government of India route for international applicants: the applicant registers for a compulsory SII ID, explores participating institutes and courses, submits applications to several institutes from one profile, accepts an offer letter, then applies for a student visa or student e-visa.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - official portal

evidence.claimText: The Bureau of Immigration directs foreign nationals who wish to apply to Indian institutes to register under the Study in India scheme, confirming the portal as a government-recognised route rather than a third-party service.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: The Indian Council for Cultural Relations administers Government of India scholarship schemes for international students at UG, PG and PhD level, including AYUSH streams; applications are handled through the ICCR A2A scholarship portal and the applicant's Indian diplomatic mission.
evidence.sourceLabel: ICCR Admissions to Alumni (A2A) Scholarship Portal
evidence.internalNotes: Portal states that applicants should contact the Indian Mission for scholarship updates - eligibility and open cycles are mission-specific and vary by country, so no scheme may be presented as open to all nationalities.

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals must obtain a Student Visa to pursue on-campus, full-time structured courses or research at educational institutions recognised by the Government of India. Student (S-3) visas cover yoga, Vedic culture, Indian dance, music and Buddhist studies at approved institutions; Student (S-5) visas cover internships.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals entering India on a Student visa valid for more than 180 days must register with the jurisdictional FRRO or FRO within 14 days of arrival. Pakistani nationals must register within 24 hours. Children under 12 years and OCI cardholders are exempt from registration, and citizens of Nepal and Bhutan are exempt from both visa and registration requirements.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Registration Requirements
evidence.internalNotes: Corroborated by the Study in India Onboarding & FRRO page, which states e-FRRO registration within 14 days of landing. Nationality-dependent rule - never state one universal deadline.

evidence.claimText: Students on an Indian Student visa must not undertake employment or business activity in India, must open a Non-Resident Ordinary (NRO) account with a recognised Indian bank and furnish the details to the FRRO, and must not enrol in off-campus franchise centres, distance-learning study centres of open universities or outreach programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India
evidence.internalNotes: Directly constrains any work-rights or earn-while-you-study claim on India pages. Do not publish part-time work guidance for India.

evidence.claimText: An applicant should possess proof of admission to a full-time regular academic course at a recognised Indian institution and evidence of financial support, and must also hold a No Objection Certificate from the Ministry of Health where the admission is to a medical or paramedical course.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Onboarding & FRRO
evidence.internalNotes: The portal adds its own disclaimer that document requirements differ across countries and must be confirmed with the nearest Indian embassy.

evidence.claimText: Admission for Foreign Nationals, OCIs, PIOs and NRIs to undergraduate engineering, architecture and planning programmes at NITs, IIEST, IIITs, SPAs and other centrally funded technical institutes runs through the Ministry of Education DASA scheme, and for the 2026-27 year admission is on the basis of JEE (Main) 2026. DASA seats are supernumerary and capped at up to 15 per cent of a programme's total seats. IITs are outside the DASA scheme.
evidence.sourceLabel: Information Brochure DASA 2026 (UG), Central Seat Allocation Board / Ministry of Education
evidence.internalNotes: The qualifying-exam basis has changed between cycles (SAT in earlier cycles, JEE Main for 2026-27). Never state the accepted exam without naming the admission year. Corroborated by dasanit.org, which describes DASA as an MoE scheme for Foreign Nationals, PIOs, OCIs and NRIs to NITs, CFTIs and other premier technical institutions other than IITs.

evidence.claimText: Non-Resident Indians, Overseas Citizens of India and Foreign Nationals are eligible to appear in NEET (UG) and are eligible for admission to medical and dental colleges subject to the rules of the respective State Governments, institutions and the Government of India. Foreign applicants must upload documentary proof of nationality with the application and are directed to confirm eligibility with the competent state and counselling authorities.
evidence.sourceLabel: Information Bulletin NEET (UG)-2026, National Testing Agency
evidence.internalNotes: Chapter 6, sections 1-2. No India medical page may present a NEET-free route. Eligibility is explicitly conditional on state and institution rules, so it varies by college.

evidence.claimText: The National Assessment and Accreditation Council, established in 1994 as an autonomous institution of the UGC, assesses and accredits Indian higher education institutions. The National Institutional Ranking Framework, launched by the Ministry of Education in September 2015, is the government ranking framework for Indian institutions.
evidence.sourceLabel: NAAC - official site
evidence.internalNotes: NIRF corroborated separately at https://www.nirfindia.org/Home (MoE, launched 29 September 2015). Use a NAAC grade or NIRF rank only with the assessment or ranking year stated.

evidence.claimText: The UGC publishes a list of fake universities alongside its lists of Central, State, Deemed-to-be and State Private universities, so institutional recognition must be checked against UGC records before an Indian institution is presented as degree-awarding.
evidence.sourceLabel: University Grants Commission - Higher Education Institutions listings
evidence.internalNotes: Operational rule for this catalogue: no Indian university is published without a verifiable UGC listing and, where applicable, AICTE approval or NMC recognition.

evidence.claimText: India spans Himalayan, tropical coastal, semi-arid and monsoon-affected climate zones, with the southwest monsoon typically running from June to September.
evidence.sourceLabel: India Meteorological Department, Ministry of Earth Sciences
evidence.internalNotes: General climatic framing only; do not present city-level weather claims at country level.
